zajjaj:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أنْ تُؤْمِنَ إلا بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ — its meaning is: "No soul has access to faith except through what Allah has made known to it of it." It may also be: "except by the enabling grace (tawfīq) of Allah", which is His permission. ﴿وَيَجْعَلُ الرِّجْسَ عَلى الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾: ”اَلرِّجْسُ“ is the punishment; and it is said: it is al-rijz.

zajjaj:103-103.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنا والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كَذَلِكَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نُنْجِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, and ”نُنْجِئُ“ [Translator's note: so written in the source], i.e. when a town is destroyed, Allah saves the prophets and the believers from what descends upon its people.
If someone says: "[Regarding] 'Why then was there not a town that believed?' — did no one among the people of the towns believe?", the meaning is that Allah mentioned disbelief concerning the majority of the people of the towns, for He said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ أهْلَ القُرى آمَنُوا واتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ ولَكِنْ كَذَّبُوا فَأخَذْناهم بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 96].
As for whoever read ”نُجِّيَ المُؤْمِنِينَ“, it has no valid aspect; [it would amount to] "the saving was given to the believers" (nujjiya al-najāʾa al-muʾminīna). This was related as a reading from ʿĀṣim in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, and it has no valid aspect.

zajjaj:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿فاليَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَن خَلْفَكَ آيَةً﴾ — ”نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ“ means: We shall cast you out naked. It has also been said that ”نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ“ means: We shall cast you onto a najwa (raised ground) of the earth. That was a sign only because he used to claim that he was a god, and his people used to worship him; so Allah made his case clear, and that he was a servant. Part of the sign in it is that the people were drowned and he was brought out from among them; so in that there was a sign.

zajjaj:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ كُنْتَ في شَكٍّ مِمّا أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ فاسْألِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — this is a verse about which people's questions have been many and their delving into it very great, yet in the sura there is what points to its explanation and uncovers its true meaning. The meaning is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — addressed the Prophet ﷺ, and that address includes all creation.
So the meaning is: ”إنْ كُنْتُمْ في شَكٍّ فاسْألُوا“ (If you [all] are in doubt, then ask). The proof of that is His saying — at the end of the sura —: ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ في شَكٍّ مِن دِينِي فَلا أعْبُدُ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ولَكِنْ أعْبُدُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفّاكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 104].
So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that His Prophet ﷺ is not in doubt, and commanded him to recite that to them. It is related from al-Ḥasan that he said: "He did not ask, and he did not doubt." This is very clear. The proof that addressing the Prophet is addressing the people is His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]: He said ”طَلَّقْتُمُ“ (you [plural] divorce), while the wording of the beginning of the address is to the Prophet ﷺ alone. This is the best of the views.
There are two other views on it. [The first:] ”فَإنْ كُنْتَ في شَكٍّ مِمّا أنْزَلْنا إلَيْكَ فاسْألِ الَّذِينَ“ is as you say to a man: ”إنْ كُنْتَ أبِي فَتَعَطَّفْ عَلَيَّ“ (If you are my father, then be kind to me), i.e. "If you are my father, then it is incumbent on you to be kind to me" — not that he doubts that he is his father. There is a third aspect: that ”أنْ“ [Translator's note: so written in the source; the particle meant is the conditional/negative ”إنْ“] is in the sense of ”ما“ (not), so the meaning is: "You were not in doubt about what We sent down to you, so ask those who read", i.e. "We do not command you because you are doubting, but so that you may increase [in certainty]", as He said to Abraham: ﴿أوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن قالَ بَلى ولَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾ [al-Baqara: 260]. Increase in firmness is not something that invalidates the soundness of one's intent.

zajjaj:98-98.t:
﴿فَلَوْلا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَها إيمانُها﴾ means: ”فَهَلّا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ ؟“ (Why then was there not a town…?). The poet said:
؎تَعُدُونَ عَقْرَ النِّيبِ أفْضَلَ مَجْدِكم بَنِي ضَوْطَرى لَوْلا الكَمِيَّ المُقَنَّعا
(You count the hamstringing of old she-camels as the best of your glory, O sons of Ḍawṭarā — why not [count] the helmeted, armoured warrior?)
i.e. "Why do you not count the kamiyy?" ”اَلْكَمِيُّ“ is the one clad in weapons [and armour]. The meaning is: "Why then were there not the people of a town who believed?"
His saying: ﴿إلا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾ is an exception not from the first [category] (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ, disjunctive exception), as though He said: ”لَكِنَّ قَوْمَ يُونُسَ“ (but the people of Jonah), ﴿لَمّا آمَنُوا﴾.
His saying: ﴿فَنَفَعَها إيمانُها﴾ — its meaning is: "Why then was there not a town that believed at a time when faith would benefit them?" This came right after the saying of Pharaoh when drowning overtook him: ﴿آمَنتُ أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا الَّذِي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بَنُو إسْرائِيلَ﴾ [Yūnus: 90].
So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that faith does not benefit when the punishment has befallen, nor at the presence of death, about which there is no doubt.
Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ حَتّى إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَهُمُ المَوْتُ قالَ إنِّي تُبْتُ الآنَ ولا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وهم كُفّارٌ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 18].
As for the people of Jonah — and Allah knows best — the punishment did not fall upon them; they only saw the sign that pointed to the punishment, and when they believed it was lifted from them.
Like that is the sick person who repents in his illness while in his illness he hopes for recovery and does not fear death: his repentance is valid. But the one who sees [death] with his own eyes has no repentance. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said, in his story: ﴿وَإنْ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ إلا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 159].
As for the accusative (naṣb) in His saying ﴿إلا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾, its like in poetry is the saying of al-Nābigha:
؎وَقَفْتُ فِيها أُصَيْلالًا أُسائِلُها ∗∗∗ عَيَّتْ جَوابًا وما بِالرَّبْعِ مِن أحَدِ
؎إلّا الأوارِيَّ لَأْيًا ما أُبَيِّنُها ∗∗∗ والنُّؤْيُ كالحَوْضِ بِالمَظْلُومَةِ الجَلَدِ
(I stood there at late afternoon questioning it [the abode]; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the camp — except the tethering-posts, which I could barely make out, and the trench [around the tent] like a basin in hard, untouched ground.)
The nominative (rafʿ) is permissible, on the sense of ”فَهَلّا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ غَيْرُ قَوْمِ يُونُسَ“ (Why then was there not a town that believed, other than the people of Jonah?), so that ”إلّا قَوْمُ يُونُسَ“ would be a ṣifa (adjective). It may also be a badal (substitute) from the first, because the sense of ”قَوْمُ يُونُسَ“ is construed on the sense of "Why then were there not the people of a town, or the people of a prophet, who believed, except the people of Jonah?" I know of no one who read it with the nominative. There is another aspect for the nominative, namely the badal even though the second is not of the same kind as the first, as the poet said:
؎وَبَلْدَةٍ لَيْسَ بِها أنِيسُ ∗∗∗ إلّا اليَعافِيرُ وإلّا العِيسُ
(And many a land in which there is no human companion, except gazelles and except white camels.)

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Yūnus
﷽
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ﴾ (Alif Lām Rā. These are the verses of the Book).
We have explained at the beginning of “al-Baqara” what has been said about ”الـر“ and what resembles it.
And His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ (These are the verses of the wise Book),
i.e. “The verses that have been mentioned are the verses of the wise Book.”

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿أكانَ لِلنّاسِ عَجَبًا أنْ أوْحَيْنا إلى رَجُلٍ مِنهُمْ﴾ (Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them…).
By ”اَلنّاسِ“ here are meant the people of Mecca. It is related that they said: “The wonder is that Allah found no messenger to send to the people except the orphan of Abū Ṭālib.”
It is possible — and Allah knows best — that they wondered at the Prophet ﷺ warning them and giving glad tidings to those who believed; the warning and the glad tidings are bound up with the resurrection and the raising, so they wondered that he informed them that they would be resurrected and recompensed for good and evil. So He said: ﴿أكانَ لِلنّاسِ عَجَبًا أنْ أوْحَيْنا إلى رَجُلٍ مِنهم أنْ أنْذِرِ النّاسَ وبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنَّ لَهم قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ (Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: “Warn the people and give glad tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord”?)
The position of the first ”أنْ“ is nominative; the meaning is: “Is Our revealing a wonder to the people?” The position of the second ”أنْ“ is accusative by ”أوْحَيْنا“. The position of the doubled ”أنَّ“ is accusative by ”بَشِّرِ“. The reading is with fatḥa, but kasra is permissible: ”وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّ لَهم قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ“, because giving glad tidings is a [form of] saying, so the meaning would be: “Say to them: they will have a sure footing with their Lord.” But it is not read so unless a transmission is established for it, because reading is a sunna (followed practice).
”اَلْقَدَمُ الصِّدْقُ“ is the lofty rank. ﴿قالَ الكافِرُونَ إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ (The disbelievers said, “Indeed this is a manifest sorcerer”) — and ”لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ“: both [are read]. They only said ”لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ“ (manifest sorcery) when he warned them of the resurrection and the raising.
[Translator's note: the source has «لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ» both in the verse and in the following phrase; the two readings referred to by "both" are evidently «لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ» and «لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ».]

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ في سِتَّةِ أيّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلى العَرْشِ يُدَبِّرُ الأمْرَ﴾ (Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne, arranging the matter): He made known to them that the One who created the heavens and the earth, and whose power is such a power, is able to resurrect them after their death.
And His saying: ﴿ما مِن شَفِيعٍ إلا مِن بَعْدِ إذْنِهِ﴾ (There is no intercessor except after His permission): no mention of an intercessor came before this, but those addressed used to say: “The idols are our intercessors with Allah,” so the mention [here] came subsequently concerning intercessors. So His saying ﴿ما مِن شَفِيعٍ إلا مِن بَعْدِ إذْنِهِ﴾ means: no intercessor intercedes except for one whom Allah approves. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَلا يَشْفَعُونَ إلا لِمَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ (and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves) [al-Anbiyāʾ: 28]. ﴿ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكم فاعْبُدُوهُ﴾ (That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him), i.e. worship Him alone.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying: ﴿إلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكم جَمِيعًا﴾ (To Him is your return, all together) indicates that the matter in [their] wonder concerned the resurrection and the raising. ”جَمِيعًا“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
And His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ (the promise of Allah, in truth): ”وَعْدَ اللَّهِ“ is accusative in the sense of “Allah has promised you a promise,” because His saying ”مَرْجِعُكم“ means the promise of return. ”حَقًّا“ is accusative on [the implied] “I affirm that as a truth (أحُقُّ ذَلِكَ حَقًّا)”. Outside the reading, ”وَعْدُ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ“ (nominative) is permissible. ﴿إنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ (Indeed He originates creation and then repeats it): it has been read ”إنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ“, and it has been read ”أنَّهُ“; with fatḥa on the alif and with kasra, both are frequent in reading. Whoever reads with fatḥa, the meaning is: “To Him is your return, all together, because He originates creation.” Whoever reads with kasra does so as a fresh start and a new beginning (istiʾnāf, ibtidāʾ). ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ بِالقِسْطِ﴾ (that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with equity), i.e. with justice.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً والقَمَرَ نُورًا وقَدَّرَهُ مَنازِلَ﴾ (It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it phases): ”وَقَدَّرَهُ“ means the moon, because it is what is measured out for knowing the number of years and the reckoning. The meaning may also be: “and He determined for them both phases,” one of them being omitted for brevity and concision, as the poet said:
؎نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وأنْتَ بِما عِنْدَكَ راضٍ والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content — though opinion differs.)

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿دَعْواهم فِيها سُبْحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وتَحِيَّتُهم فِيها سَلامٌ﴾ (Their call therein will be, “Glory be to You, O Allah,” and their greeting therein, “Peace”): the meaning of ”دَعْواهُمْ“ is their supplication; He means: “The supplication of the people of Paradise is declaring Allah transcendent and magnifying Him.” ﴿وَتَحِيَّتُهم فِيها سَلامٌ﴾ (and their greeting therein, “Peace”): it may be that what they greet one another with is “Peace,” and it may be that Allah greets them in it with peace. ﴿وَآخِرُ دَعْواهم أنِ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ (And the last of their call will be: “Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds”): Allah made known that they begin with magnifying Allah, Lord of the worlds. ”أنِ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ“ is with the lightened [أنْ], on the omission of the heavy ”أنَّ“ and the hāʾ [pronoun]; the meaning is: “that it is: praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds (أنَّهُ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ).”

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجالَهم بِالخَيْرِ﴾ (And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil, as they would hasten the good): it is related [that it means] if they were answered in supplicating against themselves and their families, like a man's saying to his son and his close friend: “May Allah cause you to die,” and “May He do such-and-such to you.” It may be that He meant their saying: ﴿فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ (then rain down upon us stones from the sky) [al-Anfāl: 32], and what resembles that. So if Allah hastened that as He hastens good for them, He would destroy them by it. ”اِسْتِعْجالَهُمْ“ is accusative on [the sense of] “like their hastening of good,” i.e. as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). The meaning is: “And if Allah were to hasten for people evil with a hastening like their hastening of good, their term would have been decreed for them (لَقُضِيَ إلَيْهِمْ أجَلُهُمْ).” It is also read ”لَقَضى إلَيْهِمْ أجَلَهُمْ“ (He would have decreed their term for them). Both are good, and ”لَقُضِيَ“ is the better of the two, because His saying ﴿وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ الشَّرَّ﴾ is connected to ﴿لَقُضِيَ إلَيْهِمْ أجَلُهُمْ﴾.
﴿فَنَذَرُ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا في طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ (But We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us, wandering blindly in their transgression): ”اَلطُّغْيانُ“ in everything is its rising and its loftiness, and ”اَلْعَمَهُ“ is bewilderment. The meaning is: “We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us bewildered in their excess and their disbelief.”

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإذا مَسَّ الإنْسانَ الضُّرُّ دَعانا لِجَنْبِهِ أوْ قاعِدًا أوْ قائِمًا﴾ (And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us, [lying] on his side or sitting or standing): the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: “When affliction touches man in any one of [his] states.” So it may be that ”دَعانا لِجَنْبِهِ“ means “he called upon Us while lying flat,” or “he called upon Us standing.” And it may be: “When affliction touches man [while he is] on his side, or touches him sitting, or touches him standing, he calls upon Us.” ﴿فَلَمّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ كَأنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنا إلى ضُرٍّ مَسَّهُ﴾ (But when We remove his affliction from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us for an affliction that touched him): the meaning is: “he passes on in well-being in the state he was in before he was tried, and takes no heed of what befell him.”
And His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ (Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do): ”زَيَّنَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ“ (active) is also permissible. The position of the kāf is accusative, as the object of [a verb] whose agent is not named; the meaning is: “Their deeds were made attractive to the transgressors thus,” i.e. “like that,” i.e. “their recompense was made to be leading astray because of their excess in their disbelief.”
[Translator's note: the source says the kāf's position is «نَصْبٌ عَلى مَفْعُولِ ما لَمْ يُسَمَّ فاعِلُهُ» ("accusative, as the object of [a verb] whose agent is not named"); the object of a passive verb is normally nominative, so the phrase is translated as written.]

zajjaj:13-13.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أهْلَكْنا القُرُونَ مِن قَبْلِكم لَمّا ظَلَمُوا وجاءَتْهم رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ وما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا﴾ (And We had already destroyed generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe): the meaning is like the meaning of His saying: ﴿فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا مِن قَبْلُ﴾ (but they were not to believe in what they had denied before) [al-Aʿrāf: 101]. Allah — exalted be His praise — made known that they would not believe even if He left them forever. So it may be that He made their recompense the sealing of their hearts, and it may be that He made known what He already knew of them. The proof that He sealed their hearts as a recompense for them is His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي القَوْمَ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾ (Thus do We recompense the criminal people).
His saying: ﴿كَأنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنا إلى ضُرٍّ مَسَّهُ﴾ (as if he had never called upon Us for an affliction that touched him) [Yūnus: 12]: ”كَأنْ“ is lightened from the heavy [كَأنَّ]; the meaning is: “as if he (كَأنَّهُ) had not called upon Us.” Al-Khansāʾ said:
؎كَأنْ لَمْ يَكُونُوا حِمًى يُتَّقى إذِ النّاسُ إذْ ذاكَ مَن عَزَّ بَزّا
(As if they had never been a guarded sanctuary to be feared — when people at that time were such that whoever prevailed, plundered.)
i.e. “as if they (كَأنَّهم) had not been.”

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying: ﴿لِنَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ (that We may see how you will act): the position of ”كَيْفَ“ is accusative by His saying ”تَعْمَلُونَ“, because it is an interrogative particle, and ”لِنَنْظُرَ“ does not govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern the interrogative. If you said: ”لِنَنْظُرَ أخَيْرًا تَعْمَلُونَ أمْ شَرًّا“ (that We may see whether you do good or evil), the governing word (ʿāmil) in ”خَيْرًا“ and ”شَرًّا“ would be ”تَعْمَلُونَ“.

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ﴾ (And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs): [بَيِّناتٍ] is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا﴾ (those who do not expect the meeting with Us say): [those who] do not believe in the resurrection and the raising. ﴿ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَذا أوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾ (“Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it”), i.e. “bring a Qur'an in which there is no mention of the resurrection and the raising, and in which there is no faulting of our gods.” ﴿أوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾ (or change it), i.e. “or replace the mention of the resurrection and the raising in it.” ﴿قُلْ ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقاءِ نَفْسِي إنْ أتَّبِعُ إلا ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾ (Say: “It is not for me to change it of my own accord; I only follow what is revealed to me”): its interpretation is: “What I have brought is from Allah, not from myself, that I should change it.”

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكم ولا أدْراكم بِهِ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكم عُمُرًا مِن قَبْلِهِ﴾ (Say: “Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you; for I had remained among you a lifetime before it”): ”عُمْرًا“, with the mīm quiescent, is also permissible. That is: I had remained among you, before revelation came to me, not reciting a book nor writing one with my right hand. This is evidence that it was revealed to me, since you knew me among you: I grew up not reading a book, and my informing you of the stories of the ancients without a book and without being taught indicates that what I have brought is revelation from Allah.

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَضُرُّهم ولا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ (And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them): the meaning is: “that which does not harm them if they do not worship it, nor benefit them if they worship it.” ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ هَؤُلاءِ شُفَعاؤُنا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ أتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِما لا يَعْلَمُ في السَّماواتِ ولا في الأرْضِ﴾ (and they say, “These are our intercessors with Allah.” Say: “Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?”), i.e. “Do you worship what neither hears nor sees nor discerns, and claim that they intercede with Allah, and so give false reports?!”

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَما كانَ النّاسُ إلا أُمَّةً واحِدَةً فاخْتَلَفُوا﴾ (And mankind was not but one community, then they differed): it was said that by ”اَلنّاسُ“ here are meant the Arabs who were upon polytheism; ”اِخْتَلَفُوا“: some believed and some disbelieved. And it was said: “Mankind was not but one community,” i.e. “they were born upon the natural disposition (fiṭra), and they differed after the fiṭra.” ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ (And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them): ”لَقَضى بَيْنَهُمْ“ (He would have judged between them) is also permissible; i.e. “Had Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — not appointed for them a term for judging between them, He would have decided between them at the time of their differing.” ”بَيْنَ“ is accusative because it is an adverb (ẓarf).

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإذا أذَقْنا النّاسَ رَحْمَةً مِن بَعْدِ ضَرّاءَ مَسَّتْهم إذا لَهم مَكْرٌ في آياتِنا﴾ (And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they have a plot against Our verses): by ”اَلنّاسَ“ here the disbelievers are meant.
And His saying: ﴿إذا لَهم مَكْرٌ في آياتِنا﴾ is the answer of the conditional (jawāb al-jazāʾ). It is like His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تُصِبْهم سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ إذا هم يَقْنَطُونَ﴾ (And if an evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, at once they despair) [al-Rūm: 36]; the meaning is: “If an evil afflicts them, they despair,” and “When We let people taste mercy, they plot.” So ”إذا“ stands in for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), just as the verb does.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكم في البَرِّ والبَحْرِ﴾ (It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea): ”هُوَ الَّذِي يَسِيرُكُمْ“ is also permissible, but I do not know anyone who read it so.
﴿حَتّى إذا كُنْتُمْ في الفُلْكِ﴾ (until, when you are in the ships): ”اَلْفُلْكُ“ may be singular and may be plural, just as ”فُعْلٌ“ in your saying ”أُسْدٌ“ is the plural of ”أسَدٌ“; and since ”فُعْلٌ“ and ”فَعَلٌ“ are of one category, it is permissible for the plural of ”اَلْفُلْكُ“ to be ”فُلْكٌ“. ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ﴾ (and they sail with them): the beginning of the speech is address, and after that it is a report about someone absent, because whoever puts the absent in the place of the one he addresses may [also] turn it back to the absent. The poet said:
؎شَطَّتْ مَزارَ العاشِقِينَ فَأصْبَحَتْ عُسْرًا عَلى طُلّابِكَ ابْنَةَ مَخْرَمِ
(She has gone far from the lovers' place of visiting, and has become hard for those who seek you, O daughter of Makhram.)
And like the verse is the saying of Kuthayyir:
؎أسِيئِي بِنا أوْ أحْسِنِي لا مَلُومَةً ∗∗∗ لَدَيْنا ولا مَقْلِيَّةً إنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well — you are not blamed by us, nor hated, if she turns hateful.)
Some read: ”هُوَ الَّذِي يَنْشُرُكُمْ“ (It is He who spreads you forth). Most of what has come in exegesis concerning His saying ﴿وَما كانَ النّاسُ إلا أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ (And mankind was not but one community) [Yūnus: 19] is that “Adam” — peace be upon him — is meant by it; ﴿فاخْتَلَفُوا﴾ (then they differed) [Yūnus: 19]: Abel and Cain differed.
And His saying: ﴿جاءَتْها رِيحٌ عاصِفٌ وجاءَهُمُ المَوْجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكانٍ﴾ (a stormy wind comes upon it, and the waves come upon them from every place): the meaning is: “from all the places of the waves.” ﴿وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾ (and they think that they are encompassed): it is said of anyone who has fallen into affliction, “he has been encompassed (قَدْ أُحِيطَ بِهِ)”, i.e. the affliction has encompassed him; and it was said: the angels encompassed them.
[Translator's note: the source writes «جازَ أنْ يَكُونَ جَمْعُ ”اَلْفُلْكُ“: ”فُلُكًا“» (with ḍamma on the lām and in the accusative); rendered above by its sense as the plural ”فُلْكٌ“ on the pattern of ”أُسْدٌ“. The original reading is «فُلُكًا».]

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿فَلَمّا أنْجاهم إذا هم يَبْغُونَ في الأرْضِ﴾ (But when He saves them, at once they commit outrage on the earth): the meaning is: when He saved them, they committed outrage. ”اَلْبَغْيُ“ is going to extremes in corruption. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says ”بَغى الجُرْحُ، يَبْغِي، بَغْيًا“ when the wound progresses into festering, and ”بَغَتِ المَرْأةُ بِغاءً“ when [a woman] commits fornication.
And His saying: ﴿إنَّما بَغْيُكم عَلى أنْفُسِكم مَتاعَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ (Your outrage is only against yourselves — the enjoyment of the life of this world): it is also read ”مَتاعُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا“ (nominative), as the khabar (predicate) of His saying ﴿بَغْيُكم عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾. It may also be that the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) is ”عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ“, and ”مَتاعُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا“ is on the implication of ”هُوَ“ (it is). The meaning of the speech is that what you obtain by this corruption and outrage you only enjoy in this world; then to Us is your return. Whoever puts ”مَتاعَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا“ in the accusative does so as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: “you enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world,” because His saying ﴿إنَّما بَغْيُكم عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ indicates that they are enjoying [it]. The meaning of “your outrage is against yourselves” is: “your acting with wrongdoing comes back upon you,” as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿مَن عَمِلَ صالِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ ومَن أساءَ فَعَلَيْها﴾ (Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself) [Fuṣṣilat: 46].

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا أخَذَتِ الأرْضُ زُخْرُفَها وازَّيَّنَتْ﴾ (until, when the earth has taken on its ornament and is adorned): it is also read ”وَأزْيَنَتْ“. ”اَلزُّخْرُفُ“ is the perfection of a thing's beauty. Whoever reads ”وازَّيَّنَتْ“, the meaning is ”وَتَزَيَّنَتْ“: the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy, the zāy was made quiescent, and so the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought in for it. Whoever reads ”وَأزْيَنَتْ“, without doubling, it is on [the pattern] ”أفْعَلَتْ“, i.e. “it brought forth adornment.” ”اِزَّيَّنَتْ“ with doubling is better in Arabic, because for ”أزْيَنَتْ“ the better form in speech is ”أزانَتْ“. ﴿وَظَنَّ أهْلُها أنَّهم قادِرُونَ عَلَيْها﴾ (and its people suppose that they have power over it), i.e. able to benefit from it.
And His saying: ﴿كَأنْ لَمْ تَغْنَ بِالأمْسِ﴾ (as though it had not flourished yesterday), i.e. as though it had not been inhabited yesterday. ”اَلْمَغانِي“ are the dwellings that people inhabit by settling in them; one says ”غَنِينا بِمَكانِ كَذا وكَذا“ (we dwelt at such-and-such a place) when they settled there.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ يَدْعُو إلى دارِ السَّلامِ﴾ (And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace): ”اَلسَّلامُ“ is Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — so Allah invites to His abode, and His abode is Paradise. It may also be — and Allah knows best — that ”دارُ السَّلامِ“ is the abode in which one is safe from calamities.

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا الحُسْنى وزِيادَةٌ﴾ (For those who do good is the best, and more): ”اَلْحُسْنى“ is Paradise, and ”زِيادَةٌ“ (more), in exegesis, is looking upon the Face of Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He. It may also be that the increase is the multiplying of good deeds, because He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ (Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof) [al-Anʿām: 160]. The statement about looking upon the Face of Allah is abundant in exegesis, and it is transmitted with sound chains of transmission (isnāds); there is no doubt about it. ﴿وَلا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهم قَتَرٌ ولا ذِلَّةٌ﴾ (and no darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation): ”اَلْقَتَرُ“ is dust in which there is blackness, and ”لا يَرْهَقُ“ means “does not cover.”

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He — concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿كَأنَّما أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهم قِطَعًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِمًا﴾ (as if their faces were covered with pieces of the night, dark): it is also read ”قِطْعًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ (a portion of the night), [with] ”مُظْلِمًا“ being a naʿt (adjective) of ”القِطْع“. Whoever reads ”قِطَعًا“ makes ”مُظْلِمًا“ a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ”اَللَّيْلِ“; the meaning is: “their faces were covered with pieces of the night in the state of its darkness.”

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهم جَمِيعًا﴾ (And the Day We gather them all together): ”جَمِيعًا“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا مَكانَكم أنْتُمْ وشُرَكاؤُكُمْ﴾ (then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, “[Remain in] your place, you and your partners”): ”مَكانَكُمْ“ is accusative as a command, as though it were said to them: “Wait in your place until We judge between you.” The Arabs threaten by saying ”مَكانَكَ“ (stay where you are!) and ”اِنْتَظِرْ“ (wait!); it is a word that has come to be used for threatening. ﴿فَزَيَّلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ (and We will separate them): from your saying ”زِلْتُ الشَّيْءَ عَنْ مَكانِهِ، أزِيلُهُ“ (I moved the thing from its place), with ”زيَّلْتُ“ for intensiveness; and it is from this, when you have removed it from its place.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾ (And sufficient is Allah as a witness): its meaning is “Allah suffices as a witness.” ”شَهِيدًا“ is accusative, if you wish, as tamyīz (specification), and if you wish, as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إنْ كُنّا عَنْ عِبادَتِكم لَغافِلِينَ﴾ (we were indeed unaware of your worship): its meaning is “we were nothing but unaware of your worship.”

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿هُنالِكَ تَبْلُو كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما أسْلَفَتْ﴾ (There every soul will experience what it sent before): ”هُنالِكَ“ is an adverb (ẓarf); the meaning is “at that time it will experience.” It is accusative by ”تَبْلُو“, except that it is not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin). The lām is redundant (zāʾida), the original being ”هُناكَ“; the lām was given kasra because it was quiescent and the alif was quiescent; and the kāf is for address. The meaning of ”تَبْلُو“ is “it comes to know by experience,” i.e. “every soul will know what it put forward.” Like ”هُنالِكَ“ is the saying of Zuhayr:
؎هُنالِكَ إنْ يَسْتَخْبِلُوا المالَ يَخْبِلُوا وإنْ يُسْألُوا يُعْطُوا وإنْ يَيْسِرُوا يُغْلُوا
(There, if they are asked to lend property, they lend; if they are asked, they give; and if they play the arrow-game of maysir, they [stake] high.)
It has also been read ”هُنالِكَ تَتْلُو“, with two tāʾs. Al-Akhfash and other grammarians explained it: ”تَتْلُو“ is from ”اَلتِّلاوَةُ“ (reciting), i.e. “every soul will read,” and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسانٍ ألْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ في عُنُقِهِ﴾ (And every human being — We have fastened his fate upon his neck) [al-Isrāʾ: 13], up to His saying: ﴿اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ﴾ (Read your record) [al-Isrāʾ: 14]. They also explained it as: “every soul will follow what it sent before.” Like it is the saying of the poet:
؎قَدْ جَعَلَتْ دَلْوِي تَسْتَتْلِينِي ∗∗∗ ولا أُحِبُّ تَبَعَ القَرِينِ
(My bucket has begun to make me follow it — and I do not like the following of the rope-companion.)
i.e. it makes me follow it, i.e. it calls for my following it. ﴿وَرُدُّوا إلى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الحَقِّ﴾ (And they will be returned to Allah, their true Master).
The reading is ”اَلْحَقِّ“ (genitive), as a description of “Allah” — Mighty and Majestic is He. ”اَلْحَقُّ“ (nominative) and ”اَلْحَقَّ“ (accusative) are also permissible. The accusative is from two angles: one of them is “they were returned truly (حَقًّا),” and then the alif and lām were added. It is also permissible on the implied form “He is their Master, truly (الحَقَّ),” i.e. “that is truly the case.” There is a third angle for the accusative: as praise (madḥ), which is: “mention their true Master.” Whoever reads ”اَلْحَقُّ“ with ḍamma on the qāf does so on [the implied] “He is their true Master, not those partners whom they set up with Him.” ﴿وَضَلَّ عَنْهم ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ (and lost from them is what they used to invent).

zajjaj:32-32.t: ﴿فَذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الحَقُّ﴾ (That is Allah, your true Lord): [this was said] after they had been brought to acknowledge [it], when it was said to them: ﴿قُلْ مَن يَرْزُقُكم مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ أمَّنْ يَمْلِكُ السَّمْعَ والأبْصارَ ومَن يُخْرِجُ الحَيَّ مِنَ المَيِّتِ ويُخْرِجُ المَيِّتَ مِنَ الحَيِّ ومَن يُدَبِّرُ الأمْرَ فَسَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ فَقُلْ أفَلا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ (Say: “Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges the matter?” They will say, “Allah.” So say, “Will you not then fear Him?”) [Yūnus: 31]. ﴿فَذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الحَقُّ﴾: since they were addressed with what none but Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — is able to do, there was in it a proof of His oneness.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا﴾ (Thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who defiantly disobeyed): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. “like their deeds, your Lord recompensed them.”
And His saying: ﴿أنَّهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (that they will not believe), i.e. it has come into effect upon them that they will not believe; so ”أنَّهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ“ is a badal (substitute) for ”كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ“. Allah made known that by their deeds they have been prevented from faith. It may also be that the word came into effect upon them because they do not believe; so ”أنَّهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ“ is a badal for ”كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ“, and the word would be the punishment they were threatened with.
[Translator's note: the source calls «أنَّهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ» a badal in both interpretations; in the second (causal) interpretation one would expect it to be construed with an omitted lām («لِأنَّهم»). Translated as written.]

zajjaj:35-35.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ﴾ (Say: “Allah guides to the truth”): you say ”هَدَيْتُ إلى الحَقِّ“ and ”هَدَيْتُ الحَقَّ“ (I guided to the truth) with one meaning, because ”هَدَيْتُ“ is transitive to those guided [directly], and to the truth it is transitive through a preposition. The meaning is: “He guides whom He wills to the truth.” ﴿أفَمَن يَهْدِي إلى الحَقِّ أحَقُّ أنْ يُتَّبَعَ أمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي إلا أنْ يُهْدى﴾ (Is then He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find the way unless he is guided?), i.e. they were made to acknowledge, and it was said to them: “Which is more worthy of being followed — the one who guides, or the one who does not find the way unless he is guided?!” It has come in exegesis that the idols are meant by it.
In ”يَهِدِّي“ there are [several] readings. Some read: ”أمَّنْ لا يَهْدْي“, with the hāʾ and the dāl both quiescent. This reading is transmitted, but pronouncing it is impossible, so I do not know how it was read; it is anomalous (shādhdha). Sībawayh reported that the like of it is sometimes spoken. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read: ”أمَّنْ لا يَهَدِّي“, with fatḥa on the hāʾ; this is correct, good and excellent. The original is ”يَهْتَدِي“: he assimilated the tāʾ into the dāl and cast its fatḥa onto the hāʾ. For those who combined two quiescent letters, the original is likewise ”يَهْتَدِي“: the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and the hāʾ was left quiescent, so two quiescent letters met.
ʿĀṣim read: ”أمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي“; in quality it is like the fatḥa on the hāʾ in quality. The hāʾ in this reading has kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was also transmitted from ʿĀṣim [as] ”يِهِدِّي“, with kasra on the hāʾ and the yāʾ — he made the kasra follow the kasra — and this is poor, because of the heaviness of kasra on the yāʾ.
It has also been read: ”أمَّنْ لا يَهْدِي“, with an undoubled dāl. So these are five ways in which this word has been read.
And His saying: ﴿فَما لَكم كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ (So what is [wrong] with you — how do you judge?): ”ما لَكُمْ“ is a complete sentence, as though it were said to them: “What do you have in the worship of idols?!” Then it was said to them: “How do you judge?!”, i.e. “In what manner do you judge?!” So the position of ”كَيْفَ“ is accusative by ”تَحْكُمُونَ“.
[Translator's note: the source has «لِنَقْلِ الكَسْرِ في الياءِ» (“because of the transfer of the kasra onto the yāʾ”); rendered as «لِثِقَلِ» (“heaviness”), which the sense appears to require. Read literally: “because of transferring the kasra onto the yāʾ”.]

zajjaj:37-37.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ هَذا القُرْآنُ أنْ يُفْتَرى مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ (And this Qur'an is not such as could be invented by other than Allah): this is an answer to their saying “Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it,” and an answer to their saying “He invented it.” The meaning is: “And this Qur'an was not such as to be invented by other than Allah (لِأنْ يُفْتَرى).” The meaning may also be: “And this Qur'an was not an invention,” as you say: “And this speech was not a lie.” ﴿وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ (but a confirmation of what was before it).
There are two views on it. One of them is that it is a confirmation of the thing before which the Qur'an is, i.e. what was before your hearing the Qur'an, i.e. a confirmation from the reports of past nations and the stories of their reports. It may also be: “but a confirmation of what is before the Qur'an,” i.e. “a confirmation of the thing which the Qur'an preceded,” i.e. it indicates the resurrection and the raising.
It has also been read: ”وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ“ (nominative). Whoever reads the accusative, the meaning is: “but it was a confirmation of what was before it”; and whoever reads the nominative does so on [the implied] “but [it is] a confirmation of what is before it,” and whoever reads the nominative says: ”وَتَفْصِيلُ الكِتابِ“ (and a detailed explanation of the Book).

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾ (Or do they say, “He invented it”?): the meaning is “Rather, do they say: he invented it?” This is making them acknowledge, in order to establish the argument against them. ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾ (Say: “Then bring a sura like it”), i.e. “Do you say the Prophet fabricated it and brought it of his own accord?! Then bring a sura like it,” i.e. a sura like a sura of it. It was only said ”مِثْلِهِ“ (like it), meaning “a sura of it,” because what was sought by this was only resemblance in kind. ﴿وادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ (and call upon whomever you can) of those who are like you in denial, even if they differ from you in [other] things; ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ (if you are truthful) in that he fabricated it.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِما لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ (Rather, they have denied that which they encompassed not in knowledge): this — and Allah knows best — was said about those who denied while they were in doubt. ﴿وَلَمّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾ (and whose interpretation has not yet come to them), i.e. they did not have the knowledge of its interpretation; and this is evidence that the knowledge of interpretation ought to be studied.
It may also be that ”وَلَمّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ“ [means] “there has not come to them the punishment to which their affair leads in denying it.” The proof of this view is: ﴿كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ (Thus did those before them deny; so see how was the end of the wrongdoers). ”كَيْفَ“ is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ”كانَ“, and ”اُنْظُرْ“ cannot govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ ومِنهم مَن لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ (And among them are some who believe in it, and among them are some who do not believe in it), i.e. among them is one who knows that it is true and affirms it, or is obstinate and displays disbelief; ”وَمِنهم مَن لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ“, i.e. among them is one who doubts and does not affirm.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَسْتَمِعُونَ إلَيْكَ أفَأنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ﴾ (And among them are those who listen to you; but can you make the deaf hear?), i.e. their outward appearance is the appearance of one who listens, but because of the intensity of their enmity and hatred for the Prophet ﷺ and their poor listening, they are in the position of the deaf. ﴿وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (even though they do not reason), i.e. even though they are, in addition to that, ignorant. This is like the saying of the poet:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, [yet] hearing.)

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَنْظُرُ إلَيْكَ أفَأنْتَ تَهْدِي العُمْيَ﴾ (And among them is one who looks at you; but can you guide the blind?), i.e. he turns to you with his gaze, yet he is like the blind, out of his hatred for you and his aversion to what he sees of your signs, as Allah — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهم كالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾ (they look at you, their eyes revolving like one who is overcome by death) [al-Aḥzāb: 19].

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهم كَأنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلا ساعَةً مِنَ النَّهارِ﴾ (And on the Day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day), i.e. what was between their death and their resurrection will seem short to them, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿لَبِثْنا يَوْمًا أوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾ (We remained a day or part of a day) [al-Muʾminūn: 113].
﴿يَتَعارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ (they will recognize one another): some of them will know others; and in their knowing one another, and some of them knowing that others led [them] astray, there is rebuke for them and the establishing of the argument against them.
﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah): it may be — and Allah knows best — that this is a notification from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He —, after He had made clear the proof concerning the resurrection and the raising, that whoever denies after this sign has lost. And it may be — and Allah knows best — that in their recognizing one another they say: “Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.”

zajjaj:46-46.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإمّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ (And whether We show you some of what We promise them): it is said in exegesis that the battle of “Badr” is meant by it. And it was said that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — informed the Prophet ﷺ that He would take vengeance on some of this community, but did not inform him whether that would be before his death or after it. What the verse indicates is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — informed him that if He did not take vengeance on them in the immediate [world], He would take vengeance on them in the deferred [world], because His saying ﴿أوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهم ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ (or We take you in death — to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do) indicates that. And He has made known how the requital for disbelief and acts of disobedience is.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولٌ فَإذا جاءَ رَسُولُهم قُضِيَ بَيْنَهم بِالقِسْطِ وهم لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ (And for every community is a messenger; so when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged): the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that every messenger is a witness over his community as to their faith and their disbelief, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْناكم أُمَّةً وسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلى النّاسِ ويَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكم شَهِيدًا﴾ (And thus We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you) [al-Baqara: 143], and as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ يا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا﴾ (And the Messenger will say, “O my Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as [a thing] abandoned”) [al-Furqān: 30].
It may also be — and Allah knows best — that Allah made known that He does not punish a people except after giving them excuse and warning, i.e. He did not punish them until the messenger came to them, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾ (And We would never punish until We sent a messenger) [al-Isrāʾ: 15], and as He said: ﴿رُسُلا مُبَشِّرِينَ ومُنْذِرِينَ لِئَلا يَكُونَ لِلنّاسِ عَلى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ (messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers) [al-Nisāʾ: 165].

zajjaj:50-50.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أتاكم عَذابُهُ بَياتًا أوْ نَهارًا﴾ (Say: “Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day…”): ”اَلْبَياتُ“ is anything that happens by night, and it is accusative as [an adverb of] time.
And His saying: ﴿ماذا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنهُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ (what [part] of it would the criminals hasten?): ”ما“ is in the position of the nominative from two angles. One of them is that ”ذا“ has the sense of [الَّذِي]: “What is it that the criminals would hasten of it?!” It may also be that ”ماذا“ is a single noun, and the meaning is: “What thing would the criminals hasten of it?!” And the hāʾ in ”مِنهُ“ refers back to the punishment, accusative, so the meaning would be: “What thing would the criminals hasten from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He?!” The better view is that the hāʾ refers back to the punishment, because of His saying: ﴿أثُمَّ إذا ما وقَعَ آمَنتُمْ بِهِ﴾ (Then is it that when it has occurred you will believe in it?) [Yūnus: 51].
And His saying: ﴿آلآنَ وقَدْ كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ (Now? And you were [before] impatient for it!) [Yūnus: 51]: the meaning is “Now do you believe?!” Al-Farrāʾ claimed that ”آلْآنَ“ is only ”أأنْ كَذا وكَذا؟!“ (“Is it that such-and-such…?!”), and that the alif and lām entered by way of quotation (ḥikāya). But what is by way of quotation — such as your saying ”قامَ“ when you name [someone] by it and make it indeclinable on the fatḥa — does not take the alif and lām.
”اَلْآنَ“ according to Sībawayh is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, as in: “We, from now (مِنَ الآنَ), will come to you,” so it takes fatḥa. [This is] because the alif and lām enter only for a previously known reference (ʿahd), and ”اَلْآنَ“ — you had no prior knowledge of it before this time, so the alif and lām entered to point to the time; the meaning is: “We, from this time, will do.” So since it contains the meaning of ”هَذا“ (this), it had to be uninflected (mawqūf), and it took fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the alif and the lām.
[Translator's note: the sentence «والهاءُ في ”مِنهُ“، يَعُودُ عَلى العَذابِ، نَصْبٌ، فَيَكُونُ المَعْنى: ”أيُّ شَيْءٍ يَسْتَعْجِلُ المُجْرِمُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ“» appears corrupt: the paraphrase given (“from Allah”) implies that the hāʾ refers to Allah, and the following sentence prefers its referring to the punishment. It is translated as written.]

zajjaj:53-53.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أحَقٌّ هو قُلْ إي ورَبِّي إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ (And they ask you to inform them, “Is it true?” Say: “Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true”): the meaning [of إي] is “yes, by my Lord.” ﴿وَما أنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾ (and you will not cause failure), i.e. you are not among those who could escape being requited for their disbelief.

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿وَأسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمّا رَأوُا العَذابَ﴾ (And they will conceal remorse when they see the punishment): these are the summoners, the leaders, the disbelievers; they concealed their remorse.

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ قَدْ جاءَتْكم مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ (O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord): He means the Qur'an.

zajjaj:58-58.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا﴾ (Say: “In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice”): the lām [of command] originally has kasra. ”فَبِذَلِكَ“ is a badal (substitute) for His saying ”بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ“, and it indicates that He means by it the Qur'an as well.

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ لَكم مِن رِزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِنهُ حَرامًا وحَلالا﴾ (Say: “Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it lawful and unlawful?”): ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative by ”أنْزَلَ“. The meaning is: “You have made the baḥīra and sāʾiba [camels] unlawful, while Allah did not make that unlawful.”

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما تَكُونُ في شَأْنٍ وما تَتْلُو مِنهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ ولا تَعْمَلُونَ مِن عَمَلٍ إلا كُنّا عَلَيْكم شُهُودًا﴾ (And you are not [engaged] in any matter, nor do you recite any of the Qur'an from it, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you), i.e. at whatever time you are engaged in some matter of the worship of Allah, and whatever you recite in that matter of the Qur'an. ﴿إذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾ (when you are involved in it), i.e. when you spread out in it; one says ”أفاضَ القَوْمُ في الحَدِيثِ“ when the people spread out in talk and plunged into it. ﴿وَما يَعْزُبُ عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِن مِثْقالِ ذَرَّةٍ﴾ (And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight): it is read ”يَعْزُبُ“ and ”يَعْزِبُ“, with ḍamma on the zāy and with kasra; its meaning is “is not remote.” ”اَلْمِثْقالُ“ and ”اَلثِّقْلُ“ have one meaning. ﴿وَلا أصْغَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ ولا أكْبَرَ﴾ (nor what is smaller than that or greater).
The fatḥa is on [the sense] “Not absent from your Lord is any atom's weight, nor the weight of what is smaller than that, nor greater”; the position is a position of the genitive, but it took fatḥa because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). Whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is: “Not absent from your Lord is an atom's weight, nor what is smaller than that, nor greater, except [that it is] in a clear Book,” and the khabar (predicate) is His saying: ﴿إلا في كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ (except in a clear Book).

zajjaj:64-64.t:
And His saying: ﴿لَهُمُ البُشْرى في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وفي الآخِرَةِ﴾ (For them are glad tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter): it has come in most of the exegesis that ”اَلْبُشْرى“ is the righteous dream which the believer sees in his sleep, and ”وَفِي الآخِرَةِ“ [refers to] Paradise. It is — and Allah knows best — that the glad tidings are what Allah has given them glad tidings of, namely His saying: ﴿يُبَشِّرُهم رَبُّهم بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنهُ ورِضْوانٍ وجَنّاتٍ لَهم فِيها نَعِيمٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ (Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him and good pleasure, and gardens in which there is for them lasting bliss) [al-Tawba: 21]; and this is indicated by: ﴿لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (There is no changing the words of Allah).
And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهم إنَّ العِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (And let not their speech grieve you; indeed honour belongs to Allah entirely) [Yūnus: 65], i.e. let not their threats, their denial and their banding together against you grieve you. ﴿إنَّ العِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (indeed honour belongs to Allah) [Yūnus: 65]: indeed dominance belongs to Allah, so He is your helper and the helper of His religion.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿ألا إنَّ لِلَّهِ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ (Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth): He does with them what He wills.

zajjaj:68-68.t: And His saying: ﴿إنْ عِنْدَكم مِن سُلْطانٍ بِهَذا﴾ (You have no authority for this): the meaning is: you have no proof for this.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
﴿قُلْ إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ لا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾ (Say: “Indeed, those who invent a lie about Allah will not succeed”): this is a complete stop (waqf al-tamām).
And His saying: ﴿مَتاعٌ في الدُّنْيا﴾ ([It is but] a brief enjoyment in this world) [Yūnus: 70] is nominative in the sense of “that is a brief enjoyment in this world.” If it were accusative it would be permissible, but it is not read so, because it would contradict the muṣḥaf.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأجْمِعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكُمْ﴾ (So resolve upon your plan and [call] your partners): it is also read ”فاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكُمْ“. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its meaning is “resolve upon your plan and call your partners.” This is a mistake, because the speech [so construed] has no point: if they were calling their partners in order to resolve upon their plan, then the meaning is “resolve upon your plan together with your partners,” as you say: “If the she-camel and her young were left, he would suckle from her,” meaning “if she were left with her young, he would suckle from her.”
Whoever reads ”وَشُرَكاؤُكُمْ“ (nominative) may conjoin it to the wāw [of the pronoun], because the accusative [object] has strengthened the speech. If you said: ”لَوْ تُرِكْتَ اليَوْمَ وزَيْدٌ لَعَلِمْتَ“ (If you were left today, and Zayd, you would know), it would be permissible; but if you said ”لَوْ تُرِكْتَ وزَيْدٌ“, it would be ugly, because you do not conjoin to a nominative pronoun until you strengthen the nominative with a word together with it.
Whoever reads ”وَشُرَكاءَكُمْ“ together with ”فاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكُمْ“ with the connecting alif (waṣl), its accusative is of two kinds. One of them is conjunction onto ”الأمْر“; the meaning is: “resolve upon your plan and gather your partners.” And it may be: “resolve, together with your partners, upon your plan.” ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أمْرُكم عَلَيْكم غُمَّةً﴾ (then let not your plan be obscure to you), i.e. let your plan be open and uncovered, as Ruʾba said:
؎بَلْ لَوْ شَهِدْتَ النّاسَ إذْ تُكُمُّوا بِغُمَّةٍ لَوْ لَمْ تُفَرَّجْ غُمُّوا
(Nay, had you witnessed the people when they were enveloped in a gloom which, had it not been lifted, would have overwhelmed them.)
[i.e.] they were overwhelmed with what is hateful, ”بِغُمَّةٍ“, i.e. with what covers them. Its derivation is from ”اَلْغَمامَةُ“ (the cloud), which covers. ”ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أمْرُكم عَلَيْكم غَمَّةً“ is also permissible, i.e. a grief.
﴿ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إلَيَّ ولا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ (then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite): it has been read ”ثُمَّ أفْضُوا إلَيَّ“. Whoever says ”ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إلَيَّ“, the meaning is “then do what you want”; and ”ثُمَّ أفْضُوا“, with fāʾ, is close in meaning to it.

zajjaj:77-77.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ مُوسى أتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَكم أسِحْرٌ هَذا﴾ (Moses said, “Do you say [thus] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic?”): this speech is a making [them] acknowledge their saying: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهُمُ الحَقُّ مِن عِنْدِنا قالُوا إنَّ هَذا لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ (So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, “Indeed this is manifest magic”) [Yūnus: 76]. ﴿قالَ مُوسى أتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَكُمْ﴾ (Moses said, “Do you say about the truth when it has come to you…”) this utterance, i.e. “Indeed this is manifest magic”? Then he made them acknowledge, saying: ﴿أسِحْرٌ هَذا ولا يُفْلِحُ السّاحِرُونَ﴾ (Is this magic? But magicians will not succeed). ”اَلْمُفْلِحُ“ is one who attains what he wants, i.e. how can this be magic when the one who brought it has succeeded?! i.e. he has won and prevailed in his argument.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
﴿قالُوا أجِئْتَنا لِتَلْفِتَنا عَمّا وجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا﴾ (They said, “Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers?”), i.e. to turn us away and divert us. One says ”لَفَتُّهُ عَنِ الأمْرِ، ألْفِتُهُ، لَفْتًا“ when I have diverted him from it; and from this is their saying ”اِلْتَفَتَ إلَيْهِ“, i.e. he turned his face towards him. ﴿وَتَكُونَ لَكُما الكِبْرِياءُ في الأرْضِ﴾ (and that you two may have grandeur in the land): ”اَلْكِبْرِياءُ“ is sovereignty; sovereignty was only called ”كِبْرِياءَ“ because it is the greatest (أكْبَرُ) thing sought in the affairs of this world.
And His saying: ﴿ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ﴾ (What you have brought is magic) [Yūnus: 81], i.e. “Moses said: That which you have brought is magic.” It is also read ”ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ آلسِّحْرُ“, and the meaning is: “What thing have you brought — is it magic?!” It is by way of rebuke to them.

zajjaj:83-83.t: ﴿فَما آمَنَ لِمُوسى إلا ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِن قَوْمِهِ﴾ (But none believed in Moses except [some] offspring among his people): it was said that he remained calling the fathers, but they did not believe, and a party of their children believed. ﴿عَلى خَوْفٍ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلَئِهِمْ أنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ (for fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, lest he persecute them): it is permissible to say ”مَلَئِهِمْ“ (their chiefs, plural pronoun) because Pharaoh is one who has companions who take his orders. ”اَلْمَلَأُ مِنَ القَوْمِ“ are the leaders whose word is referred to.

zajjaj:85-85.t: And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلْقَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ (Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people), i.e. “Do not destroy us and punish us, so that the family of Pharaoh would think that we were only punished because we are in error.”

zajjaj:87-87.t: And His saying: ﴿واجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكم قِبْلَةً﴾ (and make your houses a qibla): it has come in exegesis: make your prayer towards the Sacred House. And it was said: ”اِجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكم قِبْلَةً“, i.e. pray in your houses, so that you may be safe from fear, because they believed in fear of Pharaoh.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾ (Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way): it is also read ”لِيَضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ“ (that they may stray from Your way), i.e. You gave Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, and that brought them to error, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ (And the family of Pharaoh picked him up that he might become to them an enemy and a grief) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], i.e. “they picked him up, and his affair ended in his becoming an enemy and a grief to them,” not that they intended that he should be an enemy and a grief to them. ﴿رَبَّنا اطْمِسْ عَلى أمْوالِهِمْ﴾ (Our Lord, obliterate their wealth).
It has come in exegesis: i.e. turn their sugar into stones. The interpretation of obliterating (taṭmīs) a thing is removing it from its form and from being benefited from in the first state it was in. ﴿واشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ (and harden their hearts), i.e. seal their hearts. ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتّى يَرَوُا العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾ (so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment) is also a supplication against them.
And what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said is also possible — and Allah knows best. He mentioned that His saying ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾, i.e. “Our Lord, You gave them [this] so that they would go astray and so not believe.”

zajjaj:89-89.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما﴾ (He said, “Your supplication has been answered”): it is related in exegesis that Moses supplicated and Aaron said “Āmīn” to his supplication. In the verse there is evidence that they both supplicated, because His saying ﴿قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما﴾ indicates that the supplication was from them both. The one who says “Āmīn” to the supplication of the supplicant is also a supplicant, because the interpretation of his saying “Āmīn” is “answer [it],” so he is asking as the supplicant asks.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (and do not follow the way of those who do not know): the position of ”تَتَّبِعانِّ“ is jussive (jazm), but the heavy nūn [of emphasis] entered for the prohibition, emphasizing it, and it was given kasra because it is quiescent and the nūn before it is quiescent. Kasra was chosen for it because it comes after the alif, so it was likened to the nūn of the dual.
﴿وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ البَحْرَ﴾ (And We took the Children of Israel across the sea) [Yūnus: 90]: Allah made it dry land until they crossed it.
